distinguishing_features: Dynamic feed-forward modulation of cathodic protection current based on instantaneous electrolyte presence (conductivity/conductance), rather than merely inferring corrosion from telemetry.
Actively controlling protection current to maintain constant overpotential only during wetting events, rather than passively monitoring an impedance signature.
Deriving electrolyte conductance from the existing ICCP current source (V_drop/I) to gate current output, without adding a new sensor.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to avoid under-protection during brief high-flux wetting events while avoiding over-protection/energy waste and hydrogen embrittlement during dry phases of the splash-zone tidal cycle.
parsed.viable_reason: The stated proportionalities (J proportional to conductivity, conductivity jumping from 0 to 40 mS/cm, 10x current demand) misrepresent the physics: protection current is set by oxygen-reduction limiting current and electrolyte continuity, not by bulk conductivity, and conductivity does not 'jump from zero' once a film exists; the mechanism as written is physically implausible.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Modulating ICCP current to a measured wetting/conductance signal to avoid over/under-protection is not a routine parameter tweak on the cited monitoring art and would not be an obvious step from the closest prior art.
